coverTitle:
Five Prayers
For When Money
Keeps You Up At Night
coverDek: For the budget that won't balance, the bill that won't wait, and the provision God promises before you can see where it's coming from.

points.hook: Lord, You've fed me before I ever had a plan for how.
paragraphs: Father, I keep doing math at midnight that was never mine to solve alone — subtracting bills from a number that was never going to stretch that far on its own. But I remember the years I couldn't trace how the rent got paid, how the children ate, how I made it through a month I had no business surviving on paper. You were never on that spreadsheet, but You were never absent from it either. Do it again.
points.verseText: But my God shall supply all your need according to his riches in glory by Christ Jesus.

points.hook: I declare: lack is not my inheritance — it is only my current address.
paragraphs: I reject the shame that tells me what's in my account is what I'm worth — my value was fixed at the cross, not at the bank. Every door that's closed on me for lack of money, I call temporary, not final. I am not begging for crumbs off another man's table; I am a child with an inheritance, and I take up my seat at it now, in Jesus' name.
points.verseText: Beloved, I wish above all things that thou mayest prosper and be in health, even as thy soul prospereth.

points.hook: Notice where the money fear is actually sitting in your body right now.
paragraphs: It's not only in your head — it's the tight jaw when the notification buzzes, the shallow breath before you open the app, the way your shoulders climb toward your ears every time an envelope arrives unopened. I'm not asking you to think your way out of that tension with a verse you don't feel yet. I'm asking you to exhale once, slowly, and let Me meet You in the body that's been bracing for bad news all week.
points.verseText: Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.

points.hook: You were never meant to carry a shortfall by yourself in silence.
paragraphs: Shame about money isolates faster than almost anything else — you'll skip the dinner, dodge the group chat, let a call go to voicemail rather than admit the number doesn't work this month. But this family was built for exactly this: someone quietly covering a gap they'll never mention, a meal showing up the one week you couldn't explain why you needed it. Let your church family in before the pressure convinces you to disappear instead.
points.verseText: And all that believed were together, and had all things common; and sold their possessions and goods, and parted them to all men, as every man had need.

points.hook: Baby, lay the calculator down and let Me hold the number tonight.
paragraphs: You don't have to solve the whole month before you're allowed to rest — you just have to hand Me tonight's worry and let tomorrow's provision be Mine to figure out, the way it's always been. I feed ravens that never planted a single seed; I am not about to forget the child who's been up since five doing everything right and still coming up short. Close your eyes. The storehouse isn't empty just because you can't see inside it yet.
points.verseText: Consider the ravens: for they neither sow nor reap; which neither have storehouse nor barn; and God feedeth them.

cta.closingLine: If this met you right where the pressure is, stay close — we're praying through a new topic every week.
